Sets the voltage the walk starts from, -10V to 10V

Adds to the offset knob, one volt of starting point per volt

Note — the far end of the walk is the range knob added to the offset knob, not the range knob on its own

lines: A two state machine that steps on each trigger and puts out one of two voltages for whichever state it lands in

Sets the second of the two voltages state B can put out, -10V to 10V

Adds to the knob on that row through the small knob between them
A rising edge here steps the machine, choosing a state and then a value to put out
Holds the value chosen at the last trigger
Carries 1V while the machine is in state A and 2V while it is in state B
Goes to 5V on the triggers that land in state A
Goes to 5V on the triggers that land in state B

lines: An oscillator and distortion built on the Rossler attractor, a three dimensional chaotic system
Sets the first coefficient of the attractor, 0 to 1; the classic shape is at 0.2
Sets the second coefficient of the attractor, 0 to 1; the classic shape is at 0.2
Sets the third coefficient of the attractor, 0 to 30; the classic shape is at 5.7, and raising it folds the orbit into more loops
Sets how hard the external input pushes the system, 0 to 10
Crossfades the output from the system's own signal at 0 to the external input at 1
Sets how fast the system runs, a volt per octave about C4

Note — the y and z coordinates of the attractor are computed but the maker commented out their output jacks, so only x can be heard

Adds to the coupling type knob, one unit per volt
Bends the pitch of all five oscillators through the FM knob
Adds to the gain knob, one unit per volt
